breakingNews.headline: Trump raises global tariff to 15% after Supreme Court 6-3 ruling
breakingNews.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down Trump IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on February 20, 2026. Trump responded by imposing a new 10% global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, then raised it to 15% on February 21. The new 15% rate is the legal maximum under Section 122 and is effective February 24, 2026.

notes: BREAKING Feb 21, 2026: Trump raises global tariff to 15% under Section 122 after Supreme Court 6-3 ruling
Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs on Feb 20, 2026 - ruling they were unconstitutional
New 15% global tariff effective February 24, 2026 at 12:01 AM EST
Section 122 allows max 15% tariff for 150 days - Congressional approval needed for extension
China effective rate 34.7% remains unchanged (Section 232 / fentanyl emergency)
Mexico/Canada: USMCA exemptions still apply - goods remain at near-0% rate
India, Vietnam, EU, Japan, UK: now face 15% global tariff (previously had negotiated rates)
Postal shipments from China under 800 USD: 54% rate (de minimis exemption remains eliminated)
U.S. government may owe 130-175 billion USD in refunds for now-illegal IEEPA tariffs
